title: SaaS apps that break or misbehave behind ZIA
aliases: why is this app failing through zscaler

prose.text: "Why does this SaaS app fail, or ignore a control, behind ZIA?" reduces to one of six causes. Name the cause first; the app is the example, not the answer (the SSL side of each is in [[zia.ssl-inspection]]).

steps.label: The app refuses Zscaler's certificate.
steps.text: It cannot be inspected whatever the rule says; the options are replace, narrowly bypass, or deny: [[zia.ssl-inspection.uninspectable]], with the exemption hygiene in [[zia.ssl-inspection.exemptions]]. Developer tools and Firefox with their own trust stores are in [[zia.ssl-inspection.certificates]].

steps.label: A login or MFA endpoint is being inspected when it should not be, or bypassed when it must not be:
A bypass rule sits ahead of the inspection rule a control depends on.
steps.text: The classic case is a personal Microsoft account still working after tenant restriction was configured: [[zia.saas-apps.tenant-restriction-order]], with the profile mechanics in [[zia.tenant-profiles]].

steps.label: The identity provider checks the source IP
The traffic is QUIC (UDP) and skips the proxy path:
Someone wildcarded a shared storage domain to make an app work:

prose.text: Per-app hostname lists drift quickly and are not authored here; classify the app into one of these causes and apply that cause's remedy to the narrowest hostname or Cloud Application that fits ([[zia.ssl-inspection.exemptions]]).
